title: Mohnish Pabrai's Interview with CNBC TV18 on October 22, 2026

reader_summary.headline: Mohnish Pabrai discusses US market concentration, India's potential, and political impacts.
reader_summary.overview: Mohnish Pabrai explains that the US market relies heavily on just two companies. He suggests India offers great businesses despite tough rules, while Turkey provides cheap deals ignored by short-term traders. He also predicts flat returns for the US average over the next decade.

key_points.text: The US market value is now skewed toward just two companies like NVIDIA and Apple.
key_points.evidence_quote: The S&P 500, the value of the entire S&P 500, all 500 companies 16 years ago, 2010, was about $10 trillion. And today, the top two companies, NVIDIA and Apple, are over $10 trillion.

key_points.text: India succeeds despite difficult laws because of strong entrepreneurial energy and great export potential.
key_points.evidence_quote: India does not do well because of the laws and rules and taxes and government. It does well in spite of it.

key_points.text: Turkey offers cheap investments because short-term traders ignore fundamentals, allowing buyers to purchase great businesses at very low prices.
key_points.evidence_quote: The other unusual thing about the Turkish market that I noticed, which is very very different from the Indian market, is almost the entire market, the detailed participants as well as even the institutions are extremely short-term oriented.
